{{Top}}
[[File:TIE_target_FF7.png|thumb|right|200px|The targeting computer on [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Darth Vader's]] [[TIE Advanced x1/Legends|TIE Advanced x1]] starfighter]]
{{Quote|Luke, you switched off your targeting computer! What's wrong?"<br />"Nothing. I'm all right.|[[Great Temple/Legends|Yavin Base]] controller and [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]], the former not anticipating the latter's [[The Force/Legends|Force]] abilities during the [[Battle of Yavin/Legends|Battle of Yavin]]|<ref name="ANH">{{Film|IV}}</ref>}}
A '''targeting computer''' (also called a '''target device''' or '''fire control computer'''<ref name="IDC">''[[Imperial Double-Cross]]''</ref>) was a device used aboard [[Starship/Legends|starships]] to aid [[Pilot/Legends|pilots]] in targeting their weapons. A target was considered vulnerable when it was aligned with the electronic crosshairs of a targeting computer's gun-sights.

They could be upgraded to [[Advanced targeting computer/Legends|advanced targeting computers]].<ref name="SW:RS">[[Star Wars: Rogue Squadron (video game)|''Star Wars: Rogue Squadron'']]</ref>

==Characteristics==
[[File:XwingTargetingComp.png|thumb|left|180px|Targeting computer on a [[T-65 X-wing starfighter/Legends|T-65 X-wing starfighter]]]]

The size of these devices depended on the power of the weapon being targeted. Smaller targeting computers were used aboard one-man [[Starfighter/Legends|starfighters]], while much larger targeting computers were used to help target [[Turbolaser/Legends|turbolasers]].

Targeting computers generated a digital projection of the battlefield from the pilot's point of view, and located enemy units with various sensors. Crosshairs determined where the ranged weapons&mdash;whether [[Laser cannon/Legends|laser cannon]] bolts or otherwise&mdash;would travel, and the targeting computer also highlighted an enemy fighter, turret, tank, or other target when it came in range of the ranged weapons.
